title: Safeguarded Optimize Applier with Observable Rollbacks and Canary Gates
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a production-safe automatic applier for Optimize's batching/caching recommendations that can be gated with canary policies, require approvals for high-risk changes, and perform fast, observable rollbacks on regressions. This ticket delivers the controller, policy engine hooks, observability signals, and an approval integration to make auto-apply low-risk and auditable.

Background: Optimize suggestions currently surface batching and KV caching configuration recommendations to customers and platform ops. We want a workflow where low-risk suggestions can be auto-applied under guardrails, but all changes are reversible with clear telemetry and a human approval path for higher-risk adjustments. This reduces manual toil while protecting latency/quality SLOs.

Scope / Acceptance criteria:
- Policy-driven autodeploy controller that evaluates each suggestion against a safety score and configured canary rules per customer or cluster.
- Canary rollout primitives: percent-based traffic split, timeboxed observation windows, and fast rollback triggers.
- Approval flow: automatic for low-risk suggestions; inline approval required for suggestions flagged with "requires_approval" by the policy engine. Integrate with existing approvals UI and with the console's Rollouts page.
- Dry-run mode & simulation: changes should be first runnable in dry-run with predicted cost delta and simulated latency impact based on recent traces.
- Observable rollback: on rollback, annotate audit log with reason, link to the triggering metric and GitHub PR that contained the applied config.
- Telemetry: dashboards and alerting for p50/p95 latency, error rate, model quality regressions (via eval set), and token cost delta during the canary window.
- Throttle & rate limits: per-customer apply rate limit and global apply concurrency limits.
- Audit & compliance: every automated apply must produce an immutable audit entry (who/what/when), and allow for export to customer audit logs for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Technical approach summary:
1) Policy engine: extend optimize-service to compute a safety_score and a reason vector (e.g., potential_latency_risk, quantization_risk, cache_thrash_risk). Expose an API: /v1/policies/evaluate returning a string-encoded decision (allow/require_approval/block) and a simple rule id.
2) Applier controller: a new long-running controller (optimize-applier) that consumes suggestion events from the suggestions stream, consults the policy API, and either schedules a gated rollout or creates an approval ticket. The controller will leverage existing rollout primitives in the runtime-orchestrator and implement percent-based traffic split using runtime routing.
3) Canary monitor: reuse tracing and existing runtime metrics; add a lightweight canary evaluator that computes metrics every minute and evaluates rollback predicates (e.g., latency_p95 increase > 20% AND error_rate increase > 0.5%).
4) Dry-run simulator: a component that replays representative request prefixes against proposed batching/caching changes to estimate p95 and token cost delta using cached traces. This runs as a job and stores a short report attached to the suggestion.
5) UI / approval: Console changes to show auto-apply status, safety score, canary window, and quick-revert action. Approval hook posts back to optimize-applier and records in audit log.
6) Observability: new Grafana panels and an SLO alert that triggers if canary metrics exceed thresholds. Integrate with PagerDuty for P0-level failures.

Implementation plan / milestones:
- Week 1: Policy API prototype + unit tests. Define safety_score schema and rule catalog (Aisha + Marco).
- Week 2: Applier controller initial implementation with dry-run and simulated canary pipeline (Marco).
- Week 3: Canary monitor + rollback predicates; small-scale internal canary on staging clusters (Marco + infra).
- Week 4: Console approvals UI + audit log wire-up; create dashboards and alerts (Design/PM review).
- Week 5: Internal dogfood with a handful of non-critical customers; gather telemetry and tweak thresholds.

Open decisions / trade-offs:
- Where to compute the safety_score? Centralized in optimize service vs. pushed to runtime for local evaluation. Decided: compute centrally for consistency, but expose lightweight rule checks in runtime for emergency local evaluation.
- Rollout mechanism: runtime routing supports percent split but does not currently support simultaneous mixed configs on a single GPU rack. We may need a short-lived dual-deployment pattern. Trade-off: slightly higher infra cost during canary vs. simplicity.
- Quality evaluation: rely on a small eval prompt set during canary vs. full customer eval harness. We will start with a curated 20-prompt set per model family.

Risks & mitigations:
- False negatives in safety_score: add conservative defaults and require approval for unknown-change vectors.
- Rollback detection lag: use 1-minute evaluation windows initially; increase frequency if needed.
- Customer surprise: implement per-customer opt-out and explicit notification email for auto-applies in Dedicated/Private.

Notes & links:
- PRD (confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Optimize+AutoApply+PRD
- Dry-run prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pull/382
- Rollout controller prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-orchestrator/pull/199
- Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/optimize/canary-dashboard

Acceptance test checklist:
- Simulated suggestion in staging completes dry-run, launches 10% canary for 30 minutes and reports metrics.
- Canary metrics stable: change promotes to 100% per policy.
- Canary metrics regress: controller rolls back and writes audit entry with linked traces and PR.
- Approval-required suggestion stays pending and creates console approval task.
- Audit logs include required fields and are exportable for private deployments.
